voice.speedNote: MEASURED, not guessed. At 0.78 this voice read 145 words in 81.8s = 106 wpm, far under the brief's 140 wpm guidance. At 0.95 the same lines take 63.2s = ~138 wpm, which also lands inside the brief's '60 to 70 s of speech' window. The owner must confirm the pace by ear.

pronunciation.ISUFST: I S U F S T
pronunciation.IPOPHL: I P O P H L

voice.pronunciationNote: Applied to the text sent to synthesis only. Captions and the .srt keep the real spelling. Note that ISUFST expands to five spoken words, which is why scene 7 measures 10.9s for 19 written words. The owner confirms each name by ear.

captions.note: Captions carry explicit line breaks so the 40-character rule is checked per line, not on the whole string.

scenes.title: The problem

visual.photoCredit: JFVelasquez Floro, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
visual.subject: Garbage and plastic pollution in the Marilao River, Bulacan
visual.motion: slow push-in, 1.00 -> 1.08 scale, centred on the water
visual.why: Chosen for contrast: a wide shot with sky and riverbank, visually distinct from the detection photo in s3, which is a different frame of the same river.

scenes.caption:
Waste is reaching our rivers
every day.
scenes.narration: A citizen sees waste being dumped into a river. Who do they report it to — and will anyone ever answer?

scenes.title: One photo, Ghost Mode

visual.note: Real capture: open the camera, take the photo from the fake device (the staged photo), then turn Ghost Mode on.

scenes.caption:
One photo. The location
tags itself.
scenes.narration: With LikasLens, they take one photo. The location tags itself, automatically. And when reporting feels risky, Ghost Mode keeps the reporter anonymous.

actions.why: let the live camera stream settle so a viewer sees a camera, not a frozen frame
press the real capture control; selector verified at record time
turn Ghost Mode ON — the beat the narration describes

scenes.title: The AI reads the photo

visual.note: C1: the AI Triage step shows the REAL triage response — real material labels — instead of the hardcoded simulation.

scenes.caption:
The AI flags what it
recognises. A person confirms.
scenes.narration: Our AI reads the photo and flags the waste it recognises — here, plastic waste in the water. Nothing is final: a person confirms it.

actions.why: wait on real UI state, never a blind sleep

scenes.title: Liksi

visual.note: Open the Liksi chat bubble and send one question in English.

scenes.caption:
Liksi answers legal questions
in plain language.
scenes.narration: Liksi, the built-in assistant, answers questions about the law in plain language.

actions.value: What law covers plastic waste in a river?
actions.why: one question, one real Gemini answer
wait for the real answer to arrive

scenes.title: The LGU side

visual.note: triage (Kanban) then lgu-performance. The tickets card grid is deliberately NOT used: every card renders ConfidenceTierBadge with showScore, which prints an AI confidence percentage — on the banned list.

scenes.caption:
Tracked tickets and
response targets.
scenes.narration: For local government, every report becomes a tracked ticket. Offices are measured against response targets, and late ones show as escalations. A public record shows how quickly they resolve.

scenes.title: The public record

visual.note: Split from s5 so it can own its own app and route.

scenes.caption: A public record anyone can read.
scenes.narrationNote: No narration — s5's line already covers it. Visual only, which also guarantees no frame is empty while the voice speaks.

scenes.title: No signal

visual.note: Cut scene 6 if the queue cannot be shown honestly — brief step 14.

scenes.caption:
No signal? The report waits
on the phone.
scenes.narration: No signal in the field? Reports queue on the phone, and send themselves when the connection returns.
scenes.conditionalNote: The service worker only intercepts POST /api/reports, while the report page submits to /api/v1/ai/reports, so the app queue may never populate. Test it; cut if it does not.
